title: A model for multimodal reference resolution
abstract: Provides an early formal model for resolving natural-language names and pronouns against graphical objects in a multimodal message, explicitly treating the antecedent as potentially residing in a graphical rather than linguistic context.

admission.reason: The abstract is relevant transfer work on linguistic references whose antecedents may be graphical objects, but the capability is substantially more general and older than the closer multimodal-dialogue and text-rich-image grounding candidates in this round. It does not specifically address document attachments, scene text, regions, cells, or revised artifacts. Identity is also UNCHECKED, so it does not justify a reading slot over stronger candidates.

title: DLaVA: Document Language and Vision Assistant for Answer Localization with Enhanced Interpretability and Trustworthiness
abstract: Adds answer-localization capabilities to multimodal models for Document VQA so answers can be spatially traced back to their source locations rather than evaluated only for textual correctness.

admission.reason: The answer-localization capability is directly relevant to TF5, but within this candidate set it is dominated by papers that expose richer provenance structures: quotation-to-region attribution, answer-span-to-mask grounding, node-level evidence graphs, and page-index-plus-bounding-box chains. Reading it is unlikely to close a gap that those stronger candidates leave open.

title: Unambiguous Scene Text Segmentation With Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Introduces language-conditioned segmentation of specific scene-text instances. Referring expressions are mapped to pixel-level text regions, providing transfer evidence for grounding language to precise text-rich image regions.

admission.reason: The capability is scene-text referring-expression segmentation, so the vocabulary is relevant to gap-2, but it is narrower than the later scene-text grounding candidate that explicitly aligns referring expressions, text semantics, and visual regions. It would mostly duplicate the transfer evidence while offering less direct analogy to document or screenshot interpretation. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Transformer-based dynamic cell bounding box refinement for end-to-end Table Structure Recognition
abstract: Adds a coordinate decoder that iteratively refines individual cell bounding boxes while jointly modeling table structure. The method is particularly relevant when cell-level provenance must survive table extraction.

admission.reason: The paper improves cell bounding-box refinement within table structure recognition, but the abstract does not show semantic table understanding, provenance preservation across downstream reasoning, merged-structure handling, or workbook-level reasoning. It is a narrow extraction component and does not materially close the stated gaps. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: GRAVL-BERT: Graphical Visual-Linguistic Representations for Multimodal Coreference Resolution
abstract: Resolves cross-modal coreferences in multi-turn dialogue by jointly modeling scene objects, visual relationships, dialogue history, and metadata. It is transfer evidence for resolving message expressions against attached visual content.

admission.reason: The abstract is relevant transfer work on cross-modal coreference in dialogue, but its contribution substantially overlaps the stronger ACL 2025 candidate admitted for TF4. It does not add a document-, screenshot-, cell-, or scene-text-specific capability sufficient to justify an additional reading slot. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Not All References Resolve Alike: Fine-Grained Assessment of Complementary Cross-modal Reference Resolution
abstract: Studies cross-modal reference resolution at a fine-grained level, examining how meanings expressed in one modality are associated with entities or events expressed in another. It is transfer evidence rather than a workplace-document benchmark.

admission.reason: The abstract is too general to establish a capability that materially strengthens the target streams. It states that cross-modal references are assessed at fine granularity but does not show document grounding, text-rich visual grounding, spatial localization, or a distinct mechanism beyond other admitted transfer papers. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: General Table Question Answering via Answer-Formula Joint Generation
abstract: Treats spreadsheet formulas as logical forms for complex table question answering and jointly generates an answer and its formula. It provides evidence about formula-based reasoning but does not by itself establish full workbook-level understanding.

admission.reason: The paper provides formula-based logical reasoning for table QA, but the abstract explicitly remains at table level and does not establish workbook structure, cross-sheet references, hidden regions, formatting semantics, named ranges, or other workbook-level relationships required by gap-3. The topic words match only a subset of the required capability.

title: Semi-supervised multimodal coreference resolution in image narrations
abstract: Studies coreference resolution and fine-grained narrative grounding when a longer text is paired with an image. The setting is a transfer analogue for resolving expressions in a message against associated visual evidence.

admission.reason: Image-narration coreference is useful adjacent-domain evidence, but the abstract is less analogous to workplace attachment references than the admitted visually grounded dialogue and scene-text grounding papers. It does not add document structure, textual visual identifiers, cells, or attachment-specific grounding. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: SpreadsheetBench: Towards Challenging Real World Spreadsheet Manipulation
abstract: Introduces a benchmark built from real spreadsheet-user requests and heterogeneous spreadsheet files containing multiple tables, non-standard structures, and non-textual elements. It evaluates end-to-end spreadsheet manipulation rather than normalized-table QA alone.

admission.reason: The benchmark uses heterogeneous real spreadsheets with multiple tables and non-textual elements, so it is relevant, but SpreadsheetBench 2 in this round more directly exercises complex multi-worksheet workflows and cross-sheet dependencies. The older benchmark does not, from the abstract, add enough evidence on formulas or workbook-level relationships to justify a separate reading slot for gap-3.

title: MM-Doc-R1: Training Agents for Long Document Visual Question Answering through Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Uses a vision-aware multi-turn agent to iteratively find and synthesize information in long documents. It is relevant to cross-page evidence discovery although its main contribution is agent training rather than a complete fine-grained provenance hierarchy.

admission.reason: The paper is directly relevant to long-document visual QA, but its stated contribution is agent training for iterative evidence discovery. The candidate set already contains a benchmark with explicit multi-page cross-modal evidence chains and a traceable evidence-graph method. The abstract does not add a new provenance hierarchy, failure contract, or scaling evaluation sufficient to strengthen the open gaps.
